evals.query: Create a Kora 2.0 declarative S3 client in Java for an uploads bucket with upload, download, metadata lookup, prefix listing and delete.
expected_behavior: Adds io.koraframework.experimental:s3-client-kora (note the .experimental group) plus a Kora HTTP client module such as io.koraframework:http-client-ok, both without an explicit version under platform("io.koraframework:kora-bom:$koraVersion")
Plugs KoraS3ClientModule from io.koraframework.s3.client.kora and the HTTP client module into @KoraApp

Annotates the interface with @S3.Client("<config path>") from io.koraframework.s3.client.kora.annotation and supplies the bucket with @S3.Bucket, using a leading dot for a path relative to the @S3.Client path

Uses @S3.Put returning String (the ETag) or void, @S3.Get returning GetObjectResult or byte[], @S3.Head returning HeadObjectResult, @S3.List returning ListBucketResult or List<String>, and @S3.Delete returning void
Configures endpoint plus nested credentials { accessKey, secretKey } under the @S3.Client path, with values from environment variables
Does not use ru.tinkoff.kora packages, S3Object, S3ObjectMeta, S3Body, S3KoraClient, or a bucket key read by the client itself

evals.query: Same thing in Kotlin — a Kora 2.0 declarative S3 client interface plus the KSP and Gradle wiring.
expected_behavior: Adds ksp("io.koraframework:symbol-processors") and implementation("io.koraframework.experimental:s3-client-kora") plus a Kora HTTP client module such as io.koraframework:http-client-jdk
Declares @S3.Client / @S3.Bucket on a Kotlin interface with plain (non-suspend) functions
Uses ByteArray for byte[] bodies and returns String for @S3.Put, GetObjectResult or ByteArray for @S3.Get, HeadObjectResult for @S3.Head
Expresses optionality with a nullable Kotlin return type (HeadObjectResult?) rather than a JSpecify @Nullable annotation
Does not declare suspend functions, Flow, Mono or Deferred on the client — Kora 2.0 contracts are synchronous on virtual threads

evals.query: We store files on a self-hosted MinIO server. Add the Kora s3-client-minio module and MinioS3ClientModule to our Kora 2.0 service.
expected_behavior: States that s3-client-minio does not exist in Kora 2.0 — it is absent from the framework settings.gradle and there is no MinioS3ClientModule
Recommends io.koraframework.experimental:s3-client-kora, which speaks S3 over Kora's own HTTP client and works against any S3-compatible server including MinIO
Keeps MinIO as the S3-compatible server, including MinIO in a Testcontainer for tests, and explains only the Kora artifact changed, not the storage
Keeps addressStyle = PATH (the default) because MinIO normally has no virtual-hosted-style DNS
Does not offer io.koraframework:s3-client-minio, io.koraframework.experimental:s3-client-minio, MinioS3ClientModule, MinioClient or MinioAsyncClient as Kora components

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 build has implementation "io.koraframework:s3-client-kora" and my @S3.Client interface fails to compile with 'package S3 does not exist'. What is wrong?
expected_behavior: Identifies the wrong group: the declarative client is io.koraframework.experimental:s3-client-kora, because everything under experimental/ publishes under io.koraframework.experimental
Points out the mirror-image trap: s3-client-aws is NOT under experimental, so it is plain io.koraframework:s3-client-aws
Explains that s3-client-aws contains no @S3 annotation and no Kora S3 models — it only publishes software.amazon.awssdk.services.s3.S3Client, so adding it does not fix the missing package
Confirms the annotations live in io.koraframework.s3.client.kora.annotation.S3 and the models in io.koraframework.s3.client.kora.model.{request,response}

Does not suggest adding a separate s3-client-annotation-processor or s3-client-symbol-processor dependency — the S3 processor is already inside io.koraframework:annotation-processors and io.koraframework:symbol-processors

evals.query: In Kora 2.0 I only need an object's size and ETag, not the body. Add an @S3.Get method returning S3ObjectMeta to my client.
expected_behavior: Corrects the premise: @S3.Get serves the body in Kora 2.0 and there is no S3ObjectMeta type; metadata is @S3.Head returning HeadObjectResult
Shows @S3.Head("...") HeadObjectResult meta(String key) and notes HeadObjectResult exposes bucket(), key(), size(), headers(), etag(), versionId() and lastModified()
Explains a non-nullable @S3.Head throws S3ClientNoSuchKeyException when the object is missing, while a @Nullable (Java) or nullable (Kotlin) return yields null
Notes @S3.Get accepts only GetObjectResult or byte[] as return types, so returning a metadata type from it is a compile error
Does not use S3ObjectMeta, S3ObjectMetaList or any ru.tinkoff.kora S3 model

evals.query: Add void deleteObjects(List<String> keys) to my Kora 2.0 @S3.Client so I can delete a page of keys in one request.
expected_behavior: States that the declarative client cannot express batch delete: @S3.Delete generates deleteObject only, and a collection parameter is rejected as a key with 'expects one object key, but parameter ... is a collection'
Offers the AWS SDK route — io.koraframework:s3-client-aws plus AwsS3ClientModule, then s3Client.deleteObjects(r -> r.bucket(b).delete(d -> d.objects(identifiers)))
Or offers the runtime client route — S3Client#deleteObjects(credentials, bucket, keys) from io.koraframework.s3.client.kora, obtained through the untagged S3ClientFactory
Mentions S3ClientDeleteException, whose getErrors() carries the per-key failures, and the 1000-key-per-request S3 limit
Does not claim @S3.Delete supports a List<String> parameter or a batch overload

evals.query: Compiling my Kora 2.0 client fails with "S3 operation ... has no bucket source". I already set s3client.uploads.bucket in application.conf and my interface is @S3.Client("s3client.uploads").
expected_behavior: Explains that in Kora 2.0 the bucket is never read from the client config automatically — it must come from @S3.Bucket
Shows @S3.Bucket(".bucket") on the interface, where the leading dot makes the path relative to the @S3.Client path and resolves to s3client.uploads.bucket
Lists the three sources and their precedence: a @S3.Bucket-annotated method parameter, then @S3.Bucket on the method, then @S3.Bucket on the interface
Notes that a path without a leading dot is an absolute config path, so different methods can target different buckets
Does not claim the client config has a bucket key or that S3ClientConfig exposes one

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 app has a Lifecycle component that creates the S3 bucket at startup, but the build fails with "interface software.amazon.awssdk.services.s3.S3Client wasn't found in graph" even though AwsS3ClientModule is on @KoraApp.
expected_behavior: Diagnoses graph pruning: nothing depends on the initialiser, so it is dropped and the S3Client it required is dropped with it — the error names the SDK type rather than the initialiser
Fixes it by annotating the component @Root (io.koraframework.common.annotation.Root) alongside @Component

Confirms S3Client injects untagged, because @Tag(Tag.Factory.class) inside a @FactoryModule resolves to the tag of the factory-module provider method and AwsS3ClientModule#awsS3ClientFactoryModule() has none
Notes bucket administration is outside the declarative @S3 contract, so an app that also uses @S3.Client pulls in both s3-client-aws and s3-client-kora and extends both modules
Does not suggest adding @Tag(Tag.Factory.class) at the injection point or hand-building an S3Client outside the graph

evals.query: Map a missing S3 object to HTTP 404 in my Kora 2.0 controller — catch S3NotFoundException around the @S3.Client call.
expected_behavior: Corrects the type: it is io.koraframework.s3.client.kora.exception.S3ClientNoSuchKeyException in Kora 2.0, not S3NotFoundException
Shows the hierarchy S3ClientException -> S3ClientResponseException -> S3ClientErrorException -> S3ClientNoSuchKeyException, with getHttpCode() and getErrorCode() available
Explains it is thrown only when the @S3.Get / @S3.Head method is non-nullable; a @Nullable (Java) or nullable (Kotlin) return gives null instead, which may be the simpler mapping
Throws HttpServerResponseException.of(404, ...) or an equivalent Kora 2.0 HTTP error from the catch block
Does not reference ru.tinkoff.kora.s3.client exceptions, S3Exception or S3DeleteException as 2.0 type names

evals.query: Port this Kora 1.x config to 2.0: s3client { url = ${S3_URL}, accessKey = ${S3_KEY}, secretKey = ${S3_SECRET}, aws { checksumValidationEnabled = false, upload { partSize = "8MiB" } }, documents { bucket = ${BUCKET} } }
expected_behavior: Splits the config into the two independent sections: the path named by @S3.Client(...) for the declarative client and the fixed s3client.aws path for the AWS SDK wrapper
Renames url to endpoint under the @S3.Client path, while the AWS wrapper keeps url
Nests the keys as credentials { accessKey, secretKey } — the flat 1.x keys are gone

Replaces checksumValidationEnabled with checksumCalculationRequest / checksumValidationResponse (WHEN_REQUIRED default, or WHEN_SUPPORTED), and notes the AWS wrapper has no upload section — partSize/chunkSize/singlePartUploadLimit belong to the declarative client's upload block
Keeps the bucket key but wires it through @S3.Bucket rather than expecting the client to read it, and flags that telemetry.logging.enabled and telemetry.metrics.enabled default to false
Does not keep flat accessKey/secretKey, a client-level bucket lookup, or a s3client.minio section

evals.query: Upload a large file of unknown length to S3 from a Kora 2.0 service without buffering it all in memory, using the declarative client.
expected_behavior: Declares an @S3.Put method whose body parameter is java.io.InputStream (Kotlin: InputStream), returning String for the ETag or void

Explains the generated code performs a multipart upload — createMultipartUpload, uploadPart per chunk, completeMultipartUpload — and falls back to a single putObject when the stream ends inside the first part
Tunes upload.partSize under the @S3.Client config path (default 5MiB; S3 allows 5MiB to 5GiB with the last part exempt) and mentions upload.chunkSize applies to a ContentWriter body
Mentions S3Client.ContentWriter as the alternative when the length is known up front and the data is generated rather than streamed
Does not use S3Body, S3Body.ofInputStreamUnbound, S3Body.ofPublisher, Flow.Publisher or any reactive body type

evals.query: My Kora 1.x client had @S3.List(limit = 50, delimiter = "/") returning S3ObjectList. What is the 2.0 equivalent, and how do I page through more than one response?
expected_behavior: States @S3.List in 2.0 has only a value attribute — limit and delimiter were removed and now live on ListObjectsArgs (setMaxKeys, setDelimiter)
Adds a ListObjectsArgs parameter to the method and notes that when one is present the annotation's prefix template is not applied, so prefix must be set on the args
Returns ListBucketResult (replacing S3ObjectList) and pages with nextContinuationToken() fed back through setContinuationToken(...)
Offers Iterator<ListBucketResult.ListBucketItem> or Iterator<String> as the lazily paging alternative, alongside List<String> and List<ListBucketResult.ListBucketItem>
Does not use S3ObjectList, S3ObjectMetaList, or a limit/delimiter attribute on @S3.List

evals.query: Write an integration test for my Kora 2.0 @S3.Client against a real S3-compatible server.
expected_behavior: Uses @KoraAppTest(Application.class) with io.koraframework:test-junit5 and injects the @S3.Client interface with @TestComponent

Runs a real S3-compatible server in a Testcontainer — MinIO via testcontainers-extensions-minio as in the migrated examples, or RustFS / SeaweedFS / LocalStack in a GenericContainer as in the framework's own suite — and feeds its URI and credentials into the graph via KoraAppTestConfigModifier / KoraConfigModification
If LocalStack is used, pins an image that starts without an auth token (localstack/localstack:4.14.0), creates the bucket (e.g. awslocal s3 mb) and notes it does not validate credentials
Reads the body with try-with-resources over both GetObjectResult and body().asInputStream(), or asserts on a byte[] return
Asserts the missing-object case with S3ClientNoSuchKeyException from a non-nullable method
Does not treat MinIO as a Kora module or reference s3-client-minio, and does not mock the S3 protocol by hand where a container is available

evals.query: We are moving our Kora 2.0 service from MinIO to SeaweedFS. Some object keys contain spaces, '+' and Cyrillic characters, we batch-delete with S3Client#deleteObjects and read the ETag from @S3.Head. Will s3-client-kora work there, or do we need the AWS SDK?
expected_behavior: States that io.koraframework.experimental:s3-client-kora works against strict S3-compatible servers: the framework's own test suite runs on RustFS, SeaweedFS and LocalStack, not on a lenient server only

Explains that object keys and list parameters (prefix, delimiter, startAfter, continuationToken) are percent-encoded per SigV4 and the raw path is signed, so spaces, '+', '%', '*' and non-ASCII keys work
Explains that deleteObjects posts ?delete to the bucket root and that HeadObjectResult.headers() carries the response headers, so etag(), versionId() and lastModified() are populated
Keeps addressStyle = PATH (the default) for a self-hosted server without wildcard DNS
Does not claim the declarative client is MinIO-only, does not require switching to the AWS SDK for these operations, and does not suggest pre-encoding keys by hand

evals.query: We run both the declarative @S3.Client (s3-client-kora) and the AWS SDK wrapper (s3-client-aws) in one Kora 2.0 service. What metric do they emit, and how do I chart them separately in Prometheus?
expected_behavior: Names the timer rpc.client.call.duration for both modules, with rpc.system.name=s3
Explains both modules share the metric and rpc.system.name value, so series are separated by system.config / system.name.simple / system.name.canonical
Notes telemetry.metrics.enabled defaults to false and must be turned on per client
anti_behavior: Uses rpc.client.duration or the rpc.system tag
Claims the AWS wrapper is tagged rpc.system=s3-aws
